meta.why: Removed from the country file: web-checked and confirmed not to be published documents — synthesised meta/framing nodes, geographic areas, industries, projects, institutions. Banned by data spec 2b/2c. Kept here in full so nothing is lost.

reports.title: National Statistics and Information Authority (NSIA) institutional core
reports.description: Primary national statistical office under the de facto authorities, responsible for censuses, surveys, national accounts, prices, demographic and multi-domain socio-economic statistics where published.
reports._notes: Foundational institutional node. Data continuity, coverage and independence are severely constrained.

reports.title: Afghanistan foundational statistical-system meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from NSIA and DAB sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding the NSIA institutional core, population, national accounts, CPI, Da Afghanistan Bank institutional role and BOP into the opening foundation layer for Afghan research.
reports._notes: Opening integrating node. Data quality, coverage and institutional constraints should be carried forward in all subsequent batches.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch

reports.title: Remittance inflows framing
reports.publisher: Derived from World Bank and related sources
reports.description: Framing of remittance inflows as a critical external financing and household-income source. Remittances support consumption and foreign-exchange availability under constrained formal capital flows.

reports.title: Afghanistan agriculture–humanitarian–remittances densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from MAIL, OCHA and external sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding agriculture and wheat statistics, humanitarian needs / acute food insecurity, and remittance inflows into a coherent primary-sector, humanitarian and external-financing layer under highly constrained conditions.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
National accounts, CPI, BOP and DAB series from Batch 1

reports.title: Women’s economic exclusion and labour-force framing
reports.publisher: Derived from UN Women and labour monitoring sources
reports.description: Framing of the severe restrictions on women’s participation in education, employment and public life. Women’s labour-force participation is extremely low (single-digit employment rates in recent estimates); the exclusion is projected to impose multi-year cumulative GDP losses and is the single most consequential constraint on recovery.
reports._notes: Highest-centrality structural and human-capital constraint node under current conditions.

reports.title: Afghanistan exchange–women–border densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from DAB, UN Women and mobility sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding exchange-rate statistics, women’s economic exclusion framing, and border mobility/returnee statistics into a coherent monetary–human-capital–mobility layer under highly constrained conditions.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Remittances, humanitarian, agriculture and DAB series from earlier batches

reports.title: Afghanistan education–health–trade densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from education, health and trade sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding education enrolment and girls’ secondary exclusion, life expectancy/health outcomes, and merchandise trade statistics into a coherent human-capital and external layer under highly constrained conditions.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Women’s exclusion, humanitarian, remittances and BOP series from earlier batches

reports.title: Kabul province economic and demographic framing
reports.publisher: Derived from spatial and statistical sources
reports.description: Framing of Kabul province as the dominant urban, administrative and services centre. Concentrates a large share of the national urban population and economic activity relative to other provinces.

reports.title: Herat province economic and trade framing
reports.publisher: Derived from spatial and trade sources
reports.description: Framing of Herat as the principal western commercial and trade hub, with strong links to Iran and a large urban population. Frequently ranks among the more economically active provinces outside Kabul.

reports.title: Balkh province economic and trade framing
reports.publisher: Derived from spatial and trade sources
reports.description: Framing of Balkh (including Mazar-i-Sharif) as the principal northern commercial and trade hub, with links to Uzbekistan and Central Asia. An important secondary urban and economic pole.

reports.title: Afghanistan climate–provincial densification meta-node
reports.publisher: Derived from climate and spatial sources
reports.description: Meta-node binding drought/water-stress statistics and the Kabul, Herat and Balkh provincial framings into a coherent environmental and spatial layer under highly constrained conditions.
_referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Agriculture, humanitarian, trade and population series from earlier batches
